relationships.description: The metric instrument is created from a Meter obtained under this instrumentation scope, so it cannot exist without that scope, and every measurement it records carries the scope's name and version as its origin.
relationships.evidence: The code calls meterProvider.getMeter or meterBuilder with the scope name and version, then calls createCounter, histogramBuilder or a similar factory on that same Meter to declare the instrument.

relationships.description: The metric instrument relies on this resource to identify the service, host or process that produced its measurements, because the SDK attaches the resource to every metric stream the instrument yields.
relationships.evidence: The MeterProvider that supplies the instrument's Meter is built with this Resource, through Resource.create, resource detectors or OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES.

relationships.description: The aggregated measurements recorded by the instrument are collected by a metric reader and shipped, or exposed for scraping, through this exporter configuration to its destination backend.
relationships.evidence: The MeterProvider that owns the instrument registers a PeriodicExportingMetricReader or pull reader wired to this exporter, or a Collector metrics pipeline lists the exporter, and the instrument's name appears in the exported payload.

relationships.description: Measurements from the instrument are claimed to be forwarded as log records into this log-processing stage, which would require an explicit metrics-to-logs bridge or conversion.
relationships.evidence: A Collector pipeline or custom bridge converts the instrument's data points into LogRecords, and that conversion is configured to feed this specific log processor.

relationships.description: Values recorded by the instrument are claimed to be passed into this span, for example copied onto it as span attributes or events, while the span's operation runs.
relationships.evidence: Code inside the span's scope records the measurement and also writes the same value onto the span with setAttribute or addEvent.

relationships.description: The instrument's measured quantity is the indicator against which this outcome's target value or threshold is checked, so the time series shows whether the outcome has been reached.
relationships.evidence: An SLO, dashboard or KPI document defines the outcome's target as a threshold on this instrument's metric name and unit.

relationships.description: The instrument counts or times activations of this user control, such as clicks on the button or how long the triggered operation takes, so its usage and responsiveness can be observed.
relationships.evidence: The control's click or activation handler calls counter.add or histogram.record on this instrument, with attributes that identify the control.

relationships.description: The instrument records a health, throughput, latency or resource quantity for this application component, so operators can observe how the component behaves at runtime.
relationships.evidence: The instrument is declared in the component's own code or in its instrumentation library and is recorded from the component's methods, with attributes such as the component or service name.

relationships.description: The instrument measures the request rate, error rate or duration of the operations this application service offers, so its consumers' experience can be tracked.
relationships.evidence: The handlers that implement the service's operations record to this instrument, for example an http.server.request.duration histogram labelled with the service's operations.

relationships.description: The instrument records a business-level quantity for this process, such as completed instances, cycle time or failed steps, so process performance can be observed from telemetry.
relationships.evidence: The code that implements the process's activities or its completion event records to this instrument, and a business dashboard charts the metric under the process name.

relationships.description: The instrument provides a measured indicator of how well this business service is delivered, such as orders fulfilled, claims handled or delivery latency.
relationships.evidence: A service-level dashboard or SLO for the business service queries this instrument's metric, and the systems that realize the service record to it.

relationships.description: The instrument measures activity or state of this stored collection, such as query latency, row or document counts, or write throughput against that table, bucket or index.
relationships.evidence: Database client instrumentation or custom code records to this instrument with a db.collection.name or table attribute equal to the collection's name.

relationships.description: The instrument tracks the health and load of this database, such as connection pool usage, operation duration or error counts at its endpoint.
relationships.evidence: The instrument, for example db.client.operation.duration or a connection-count metric, is recorded with db.namespace or server.address attributes that identify this database's connection.

relationships.description: The instrument counts how often the failure display defined by this error configuration is shown to users, broken down by severity or message.
relationships.evidence: The error-handling code that applies this configuration to show the notification or fallback message also calls counter.add on the instrument, with attributes for the error type.

relationships.description: The instrument counts or times occurrences of this route change, such as how often users move from the source route to the destination route and how long the transition takes.
relationships.evidence: A router guard or navigation hook, such as afterEach or a router event subscription, records to the instrument with attributes for the source and destination routes.

relationships.description: The instrument measures a quantity about instances of this structured record type, such as how many are created, how many fail validation, or their payload size.
relationships.evidence: Code that validates, persists or serializes instances of the entity or DTO records to the instrument, with an attribute naming the schema or type.

relationships.description: The instrument records request count, latency or error rate for this specific method and path pair, so each API endpoint's behaviour can be observed.
relationships.evidence: The route handler for the operation, or HTTP server middleware, records to the instrument with http.request.method and http.route attributes that match the operation.

relationships.description: The instrument records aggregate traffic or latency across all HTTP methods served under this URL path template.
relationships.evidence: The instrument is recorded with an http.route attribute equal to the path template, and a dashboard aggregates the metric across methods for that path.

relationships.description: The instrument measures user visits to this client-side route or its load and render time, such as page views or lazy-load duration.
relationships.evidence: Router instrumentation or a route-level hook records to the instrument with an attribute carrying the route's path pattern.

relationships.description: The instrument measures a quantity about data conforming to this reusable schema definition, such as validation failures or the volume of payloads of that type.
relationships.evidence: The validation or serialization code that resolves '#/definitions/{name}' records to the instrument, with an attribute naming that definition.

relationships.description: The instrument observes the availability, utilization or latency of this infrastructure capability, such as cache hit ratio, queue depth or storage throughput.
relationships.evidence: The instrument is recorded by client instrumentation or host metrics for the platform service, with attributes such as messaging.system or the cache name that identify that service.

relationships.description: The instrument serves as a detection signal for this threat, counting events that indicate it is happening, such as failed login bursts for credential stuffing or rejected injection payloads.
relationships.evidence: The security-relevant code path, such as the authentication failure handler or the input sanitizer rejection, records to the instrument, and an alert rule on the metric references the threat.

relationships.description: The instrument measures load time, render performance or usage of this top-level UI surface, such as how long the page takes to become interactive or how often it is opened.
relationships.evidence: The view's mount or load lifecycle hook, or web-vitals instrumentation, records to the instrument with an attribute naming the view.

relationships.description: The instrument is claimed to make this qualitative stakeholder goal concrete by providing the observable measurement through which progress toward it is made tangible.
relationships.evidence: Architecture or OKR documentation traces the goal to this instrument as its implemented measurement, and a dashboard reports the goal using the instrument's metric.

relationships.description: Measurements from the instrument point to this span by reference, typically as exemplars that carry the span's trace and span IDs, without depending on the span to function.
relationships.evidence: Exemplar sampling is enabled for the instrument, and the exported data points carry exemplar trace and span IDs that belong to spans with this span's name.

relationships.description: The instrument fulfils an observability requirement, for example 'the system shall record checkout latency', by providing exactly the required measurement with the required unit and kind.
relationships.evidence: The requirement's acceptance criteria name the metric, and the codebase declares an instrument with that name, kind and unit, which a test or review confirms.

notes: flows-to logprocessor and flows-to span are semantically wrong: metrics flow to readers or exporters, not to log processors or spans. Exemplar links are already covered by references span. realizes goal should be supports-goals. maps-to outcome should be measures-outcome. monitors pathitem is redundant with monitors operation. Monitoring errorconfig, threat and the schema types is indirect at best.
